title: Redwood technical deep dive - Dedicated vs Hosted (OptiRetail)
summary: SE-led deep dive on runtime performance tradeoffs between Redwood Dedicated and Hosted. Focus on noisy neighbor isolation, throughput guarantees, KV caching strategies, batching, quantization impacts, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed next step: run 1-day benchmark on dedicated cluster and send security/compliance packet.
next_steps: Redwood to share security/compliance packet and SOC2 docs (Alex)
Schedule 1-day throughput/latency benchmark on Dedicated with OptiRetail model (Priya to coordinate)
Provide cost estimate for Dedicated reserved pool and hosted fallbacks (Alex)
OptiRetail to provide sample workload traces and model binary (if allowed) (Maya)
action_items: Alex Chen: Share security/compliance packet + SOC2, ISO docs by 2026-05-24
Priya Singh: Draft benchmark plan and tooling list by 2026-05-23
Maya Lopez: Send anonymized workload traces and model spec by 2026-05-26
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex, AE on the Redwood account, Priya's our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Maya Lopez: Good, thanks. We want to dig straight into performance. We run a recommendation model, latency 50-150ms P50, P95 around 300ms today. We're evaluating Dedicated vs hosted for isolation and cost.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Great. So I'll start with a quick overview of how our runtime behaves on Hosted vs Dedicated, then we can jump into KV cache, batching, and quantization numbers. Quick clarifying question — is the model you plan to serve a decoder-only LLM or an encoder-decoder? And approx size?
[00:33] Jordan Kim: Decoder-only, about 30B params, mixed precision trained, we currently serve FP16. Throughput on our infra maxes at about 40-50 rps with 16k tokens session lengths for bulk workloads.
[00:45] Priya Singh: OK. On Hosted we multi-tenant across customers on GPU pools; we provide performance profiles but no hard throughput guarantees. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, predictable throughput, and can be configured with reserved capacity and SLA-backed latency/uptime. The key tradeoff is cost vs absolute isolation.
[01:02] Samir Patel: Can you explain noisy neighbor scenarios? How often do we see degradation on Hosted and what mitigation exists?
[01:09] Priya Singh: Sure. Noisy neighbor is when other tenants consume disproportionate GPU cycles or memory, causing scheduling delays or contention for networking. In our hosted infra we mitigate with soft QoS, request shaping, and automated routing to alternate pools. But there are cases during massive peaks where P95 tails inflate; that's rare but it happens. Dedicated removes that class of risk since your workloads live on reserved hardware.
[01:32] Maya Lopez: What's the expected P95 variance on Hosted vs Dedicated for a 30B model at our token lengths?
[01:38] Priya Singh: Based on our benchmarks, Hosted P50 is often comparable to Dedicated; P95 on Hosted can be 1.8-2.5x Dedicated during noisy periods. On Dedicated we aim for <1.2x variance day-to-day assuming autoscaling policy and buffering are tuned. We'll run the optiretail workload to give you exact numbers.
[01:55] Jordan Kim: About KV cache — we rely heavily on prefix caching for sessions. How is KV cache shared or persisted on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:03] Priya Singh: KV cache is per-worker process. On Hosted it's ephemeral — cached per request worker and we have mechanisms for prefix reuse across similar sessions, but persistence across requests depends on routing consistency. On Dedicated you control routing and can pin sessions to nodes, so you get higher cache hit rates and lower token recomputation. Also Dedicated can be configured with larger KV storage and longer-lived workers.
[02:24] Alex Chen: To add: we also offer a managed Redis-like external cache in private deployments for very large stateful sessions if that's a requirement.
[02:31] Maya Lopez: Interesting. For batching: we have tight latency SLOs, we can't batch for more than 30ms extra. How do you balance batching benefits vs latency?
[02:40] Priya Singh: Redwood uses continuous batching where we trade a small, bounded wait to aggregate compatible requests. We tune batch windows per route; for your SLO we can set micro-batch windows of 10-30ms and fall back to low-latency path if not enough requests accumulate. Dedicated gives you more control to increase batch sizes for throughput peaks.
[02:57] Jordan Kim: Quantization — we want to reduce cost. What's the impact of INT8 or 4-bit on quality for our recommendation model?
[03:05] Priya Singh: Quantization depends on model architecture. For many decoder-only Transformer models, INT8 with per-channel quantization gives big memory reductions with minimal degradation, often <1-2% metric drop on ranking tasks. 4-bit and extreme quantization are higher risk; we run evals with guardrails and fallback to FP16 for critical queries. We can run A/B evals on your holdout.
[03:24] Maya Lopez: If we quantize aggressively on Dedicated, can we still use Hosted fallback if quality drops?
[03:29] Priya Singh: Yes. Our routing can detect quality regressions and route to a higher-precision variant (FP16) in Hosted or another Dedicated pool. That's part of our automatic fallback policies.
[03:38] Samir Patel: Network: For VPC/on-prem, what's the network egress path and can we keep data in-region?
[03:45] Alex Chen: For Redwood Private (VPC), control plane is in customer VPC and data stays in their region. On-prem options keep traffic within the network; we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management so plaintext never leaves your KMS boundary if you choose that mode.
[04:01] Jordan Kim: SLAs — if we buy Dedicated reserved pool, what throughput guarantees exist? We need consistent tail latencies at P99 for online inference.
[04:10] Priya Singh: With Dedicated reserved capacity, we provide throughput SLAs tied to the reserved GPU count. For P99 we offer higher targets — we also expose token-level traces in Console so you can track if your SLOs are being met. The SLA specifics depend on contract (we can share a sample). For hard realtime requirements we recommend a slightly overprovisioned pool plus autoscale buffer.
[04:32] Maya Lopez: Any tips to improve P99 aside from overprovisioning?
[04:36] Priya Singh: Yes — prefix caching, session pinning, quantization where acceptable, and smart batching policies. Also warm workers for cold-start sensitive models and keep-alive pooling reduce jitter.
[04:48] Jordan Kim: What's the warm-up profile? How long to load the model into memory and warm KV caches?
[04:54] Priya Singh: Model load times depend on format and quantization; a 30B FP16 model typically loads in 90-150s on modern GPUs; INT8 can be slightly faster due to smaller memory footprint. KV caches warm as sessions run; with pinning you get near-instant reuse for multi-request sessions.
[05:10] Maya Lopez: For compliance, we need audit logs and per-token data retention control; Hosted retains logs for 30 days by default. Can we change that?
[05:18] Alex Chen: Yes, per contract. Hosted default is 30 days but we offer longer retention or deletion policies, and Dedicated/Private gives you complete control. We also provide audit logs and SSO/SAML integrations and can integrate with your SIEM.
[05:31] Jordan Kim: Cost sensitivity — can you give rough cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our expected 50 rps peak?
[05:38] Alex Chen: Ballpark: Hosted per-token pricing is cheaper at low commitment but at sustained 50 rps across day Dedicated reserved capacity with a 3- or 12-month commit typically reduces per-token cost by 30-50% depending on utilization. We'll provide a detailed cost model after we see your traces.
[05:55] Samir Patel: Any pitfalls for on-prem deployment — ops burden?
[05:59] Priya Singh: On-prem increases ops overhead; we provide an appliance and runbooks, but you'll need infra to manage GPU lifecycle, kernel dependencies, and network. We offer support tiers for private installs.
[06:11] Maya Lopez: We might start with Hosted and move to Dedicated. Do you support lifting the same model + routing configs between Hosted and Dedicated seamlessly?
[06:18] Priya Singh: Yes — that's a core Redwood promise. Same API, same routing, same rollouts. You can pin model versions and have canary flows across environments.
[06:27] Alex Chen: Ok let's recap and action items — Priya will run the benchmark plan, Alex will share security docs and pricing, Maya will send traces. Any final quick questions?
[06:38] Maya Lopez: On the benchmark, can we include both FP16 and INT8 runs and see quality regressions automatically?
[06:44] Priya Singh: Absolutely. We'll include eval harness and threshold alerts.
[06:48] Jordan Kim: Also please include a KV cache hit rate breakdown and latency breakdown by token position.
[06:53] Priya Singh: Will do.
[06:56] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the packet and calendar invite for the benchmark kick-off.
[07:03] Maya Lopez: Thanks, bye.
[07:05] Samir Patel: Thanks!
